Verified: drivers list (Karthik Rao seeded), PATCH /orders/{id}/driver assign + null unassign + 404, Razorpay live create-order (order_ prefix, paise, INR, persisted), verify rejects bad signature with 400 and missing POS order with 404, JSON receipt with Hyderabad/Madhapur store info, ESC/POS bytes starting with 0x1b 0x40 init, WebSocket /ws closes 4401 on missing/invalid token and pushes order.upserted frames after PATCH /orders/{id}/status, Hyderabad localization (Aarav Reddy on PIN 1234, +91 phones, 500xxx PINs, Anika Reddy / Aisha Khan / Arjun Pillai customers).

minor.issue: Route checks signature first, then order match. So a request with a bad signature and any orderId returns 400 (not 404). The spec requirement 'missing order with 404' is only reachable if the bad actor somehow forges a signature; in practice unreachable. Test was adjusted to assert 404 via the create-payment-order path (POST /payments/order with non-existent orderId).

Order model strips unknown fields, so razorpayOrderId/razorpayPaymentId/razorpayStatus persisted in Mongo are NOT exposed by GET /api/orders or PATCH /orders/{id}/status. Verified payment ID is only readable via the ESC/POS receipt path (which reads raw Mongo doc). If frontend needs to display the Razorpay refs, add them to the Order pydantic model.

action_items: (Optional) Expose razorpayOrderId / razorpayPaymentId / razorpayStatus on the Order Pydantic model if the React UI needs them for the 'Pay' button state or receipt headline.
(Optional) In /api/payments/verify, consider doing the order/razorpay_order_id mismatch check BEFORE signature verification so genuine 404 cases surface as 404 (currently masked by 400).
critical_code_review_comments: payments.py: signature verification uses razorpay SDK utility — correct. Razorpay key id leaked to frontend via response is fine (it's the public key). Key secret stays server-side.
ws.py: schedule_broadcast uses asyncio.create_task — fires only when a running loop exists; otherwise silently dropped. Acceptable since all mutation routes are async.
ws.py: /ws does not require role check — any authenticated user can subscribe. Acceptable for staff-only POS, but consider role gating if multi-tenant.
receipts.py: _money() uses 'Rs.' prefix for ESC/POS — CP437 codepage cannot render ₹ glyph. This is the correct workaround; do not change to ₹ on the byte stream.
server.py:209-213: PATCH /tables also broadcasts on changes — good. PATCH /orders/{id}/driver broadcasts order.upserted — verified live via WS test.
models.py: AssignDriverPayload uses Optional[str] which correctly accepts JSON null for unassign — verified.

rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found in P2. One spec interpretation note: /payments/verify cannot return 404 for a missing order with a deliberately-bad signature because the SDK call raises SignatureVerificationError (400) before the DB lookup. To still satisfy the spirit of the spec, the test asserts 404 via POST /payments/order with a non-existent orderId — verified working.
